newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares recoup losses, end up 0.25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares recoup losses, end up 0.25 pct.

text.p: Brazil shares absorbed early profit-taking to end up a slight 0.25 percent in thin trade, with players rolling over positions due to a U.S. holiday, brokers said.
"It's a holiday in New York; nothing happened," said a trader noting that there was a lack of foreign interest in today's session.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most traded shares ended up 191 points at 78,354 points. Turnover was thin at 208.2 million reais ($199.7 million).
Brazilian stocks are expected to open higher Tuesday, with investors awaiting the release of Brazil trade figures for 1996, analysts said.

They said the market expects Brazil to post a trade deficit of around $5.5 billion in 1996. Earlier today, local wire reports quoted a Industry and Commerce Ministry official as saying Brazil trade deficit would reach $5.6 billion in 1996.
Investors will also be eyeing Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony on Tuesday, they added.

Benchmark Telebras preferred shares ended up 0.11 percent at 89.60 reais. Power company Eletrobras preferred shares rose 1.18 percent to close at 429 reais. Mining firm Vale do Rio Doce preferred stock fell 0.85 percent to end at 24.64 reais. Oil monopoly Petrobras closed at 195 reais, up 0.52 percent.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE of the nine most liquid power shares rose 0.32 percent to end at 2,259 points.
The market's wider Brazil index (IBX) of 100 leading shares also rose 0.27 percent to close at 1,697 points.
